title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's third axiomatisation of 'analysis situs' (June 1986). There is a set of strata M, a set of flags or 'types' F, and a set L of 'lieux'. All carry a symmetric 'disjunction' relation F || G. For a part A one wants a support supp A and a cosupport. These live in an ordered set Σ equipped with a 'complement' operation C. On pp. 63-64 he was puzzled whether Σ behaves like a Boolean algebra, i.e. whether A ⊂ B ⇔ A ∩ C(B) = ∅ and whether ∩ distributes over ∨.

Page 67 settles the 'quasi-set-theoretic' case. There F || G ⇔ ouv F ∩ ouv G = ∅, so Σ_L = 𝔓(L), C is the ordinary complement, and supp A = ∪_{F∈A} ouv(F).

Page 68 generalises this. He chooses a set ℙ ⊂ L of 'points' (in practice types in L) with two properties:
(a) distinct points are disjoint, so on ℙ the relation x || y simply means x ≠ y;
(b) disjunction is detected by points: for F, G in F (resp. M, passing to strata), F || G holds iff no point x ∈ ℙ lies in both ouv_Λ(F) and ouv_Λ(G), with Λ = ℙ.
Several crossed-out attempts precede this formulation, and the margin note 'Un peu bref!' ('a bit brief!') shows he found it too terse.

Conclusion: the ordered set of supports Σ_F (or Σ_M, or Σ_L) is isomorphic to 𝔓(ℙ). The map is A ↦ {x ∈ ℙ | x lies in the 'open' of A}. It is an isomorphism of ordered sets compatible with C, which becomes the ordinary complement in ℙ. So the perplexities dissipate here too, and one should define supp A = ouv_Λ A = ∪_{F∈A} ouv_Λ(F).

Modern reading: (L, ||) is an orthogonality space and Σ its lattice of orthoclosed (biorthogonal) sets with orthocomplement. Conditions (a)+(b) say there is an orthogonal family of atoms that separates orthogonality. Then for a point x, x || F ⇔ x ∉ ouv(F), so A^⊥ corresponds to the complement of A's point set. Hence Σ ≅ 𝔓(ℙ) as ortholattices, i.e. Σ is a complete atomic Boolean algebra. The next page draws the moral: outside this quasi-set-theoretic case the notion of support is probably 'caduque' (obsolete). He illustrates this with strata of an ordered segment, where the axioms hold except divisibility.
errors: The statement is sketchy, as Grothendieck himself notes ('Un peu bref!'). The final version of (b) is only legible through crossed-out drafts.

Implicitly, points must be minimal: nothing other than x itself may lie 'under' a point x without being disjoint from it. This is needed to get x || F ⇔ x ∉ ouv(F) from (b), and it is not stated explicitly.
Σ is never defined on this page (presumably closed parts for the disjunction Galois connection, from earlier pages). The claimed isomorphism depends on that definition.
Under these assumptions the argument appears correct.

ideas.what: Abstract disjunction (orthogonality) relation on strata/flags. Supports are elements of the ordered set Σ of closed parts, with a complement operation; the question is when Σ is Boolean.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space and its complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed subsets

ideas.what: A family of pairwise disjoint 'points' that detects disjointness gives Σ ≅ 𝔓(ℙ), compatible with complement, and supports become unions of point-sets.
ideas.modern_name: Atomistic Boolean ortholattice / spatial (enough points) condition; representation as a powerset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Tarski: complete atomic Boolean algebras are powersets)

ideas.what: Diagnosis that 'support' is a well-behaved notion only in the quasi-set-theoretic (point-detected) case. In general one should restrict to mutually compatible families (continued on p. 69).
ideas.modern_name: Failure of distributivity / non-Boolean orthologic for supports in stratified combinatorics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'perplexities' about supports and complements in his combinatorial analysis situs are exactly the question of when an orthogonality space's ortholattice is Boolean. This is the quantum-logic / Foulis-Randall framework. His resolution, that a separating family of orthogonal points gives a powerset, is the classical criterion. The link between tame-topology axiomatics and orthogonality-space theory seems not to have been drawn.
missed.quote: a) si x, y ∈ ℙ, x ≠ y ⇒ x || y ... Alors l'ens. ordonné des supp s'identifie à Σ_ℙ ≃ 𝔓(ℙ) ... iso d'ens. ordonnés, compatible à l'application C ("complémentaire")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could inform anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs axioms. The mathematics itself is routine, so the interest is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, self-acknowledged sketchy generalisation (powerset representation when points detect disjointness). Its interest lies in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatics and its unremarked kinship with orthogonality spaces, not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'supp A = comb_∧ A = ∪ comb_∧(F)' should read roughly 'supp A = ouv_Λ A = ∪_{F∈A} ouv_Λ(F)'. 'ouv' as on p. 67, with subscript Λ (Λ = ℙ, cf. crossed line 'le cas Λ = ℙ').
'(resp. 𝒰, si on passe à 𝒰̌)' is more likely '(resp. M, si on passe à M)', i.e. strata.
'Σ_F (ou 𝒰, ou L)' should be 'Σ_F (ou M, ou L)'.
'mais pratiquement on se. types ⊂ L je présume' is probably 'mais pratiquement on se [bornera aux] types ⊂ L je présume'.
Crossed-out lines contain 'ouv' (not 'comb'), e.g. '∀x ⊂ ouv_Λ(F), y ⊂ ouv_Λ(G)' and 'x ∈ ouv_Λ A et ouv_Λ B'.
'(dans un ℙ, x||y équivaut[?] x≠y)': the reading 'équivaut à x ≠ y' is confirmed by the image.
